title: Verify physical read work before claiming scan elimination
applies_when: A storage optimization replaces a high-level row-ID predicate with a lower-level take, or imports an older-version speedup attributed to eliminating a scan.
lesson: Resolve the actual locked dependency and inspect its planner before estimating saved work. LanceDB 0be3ae96 pins Lance e5a3553b, whose scanner lowers positive row-ID membership into a mask-based take. The reusable native probe executes legacy/stable ID requests against 512/65,536-row tables and asserts three reader rows versus full-scan positive controls. This refutes the full-row-scan premise for that route, not all possible direct-read optimizations. Next measure matched planning/materialization costs instead of assuming the logical filter implies linear work. Preserve membership, projection, snapshot and buffered-data semantics before benchmarking.
avoid_when: rows_scanned counts batches returned by the fragment reader; it does not measure fetched bytes, page decompression, cold IO or a physical performance ceiling. Four small same-schema cases do not qualify MemWAL, remote execution, compaction or all builder features. No current latency or Scout conversion benefit is established. Other versions may choose different plans.

evidence.note: Exact dependency pin; older downstream benchmarks are not automatically current-API evidence.
The scanner recognizes take-shaped predicates and dispatches to take_source rather than treating every filter as a full scan.
Defines the reader-row counter's scope; not a bytes or timing counter.
Reusable native contract and physical-work assertions for the exact LanceDB pin; requires unchanged production and declared dependencies. No benchmark.
